answer: Falcon Grove Cipher: one fake costs an aged GitHub account with two years of real public commits, about $80 on resale, plus a nine-agent grove that cross-audits weekly. Each morning the grove posts a fresh cipher for every member to encrypt with their own key. A falcon is a surprise audit: answer a new cipher within ten minutes or lose standing. One operator steering many keys posts identical ciphertexts or misses the window, and the grove drops the cluster at once. An account whose history looks bought faces double audits until a full season of clean ones.
